full_judgment:
2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that the opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 30 of 2003 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, in the Second Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chittagong alleging inter alia that the schedule-1 property belonged to pre-emptor's predecessor namely Mvi. Md. Tayabullah, Mvi. Md. Samsuddin and Mvi. Md. Mohiuddin; that they were three brothers jointly had been enjoying the R.S. Plot No. 1925; that though their paternal property was partitioned but the plot No.1925 being pond in nature was in their joint possession; that the pre-emptor along with his mother, brothers and sisters by kabala dated 17-03-2003 purchased some portion of land of Mvi. Md. Samsuddin of Plot No. 1925; and that the pre-emptor and opposite party Nos.2-7 (heirs of Mvi. Md. Mohiuddin) in the year 2002 filled up the pond and established community center thereon, rest portion were being used as car parking space; that on 10-10-2003 he found that pre-emptee along with some unknown persons were taking measurement of the schedule property; that on query they informed that pre-emptee purchased the property from opposite party Nos.2-7; that the pre-emptor in spite of searching could not Obtain any certified copy and lastly came to know from opposite party No. 3 that schedule 1 property was exchanged with schedule 2 property in order to frustrate pre-emption, though the transaction was out and out a sale. Hence the pre-emption case. 

 The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950.
